# airship

> A visual editor for the web app you are already running. Airship puts an
> infinite design canvas in front of your dev server — no plugin, no config.
> Point at any element, describe the change in plain English, and Claude Code,
> OpenAI Codex or OpenCode edits the source file, with streaming status, inline
> diffs and undo.

## What it is

A CLI. `npx @airshiplabs/cli --target 3000` starts a universal reverse proxy in
front of the dev server you already have and opens the editor on the next port.
Nothing is added to your dependencies, your config or your bundle.

## How it works

- **Reverse proxy, not a plugin.** Works with Vite, Next, Remix, Rails —
  anything serving HTML over HTTP. `--target` is the only flag most projects
  need, and it is detected from your package.json when you leave it off.
- **Frames are real viewports.** Each frame is a same-origin iframe at a device
  size, so a 393px frame reports `innerWidth === 393` at any zoom. Media and
  container queries fire per frame.
- **Edits go to source.** A picked element resolves back to the file and line
  that rendered it. Your prompt, the selection and any inspector tweaks reach
  the agent, which edits the file; you get the diff and an undo.
- **Inline mode.** `?__airship=inline` injects the overlay straight into the
  app's own page instead of the canvas shell.

## Agents

Selected with `--agent`, or switched per turn from the composer. They are not
equivalent:

- **claude** (default) — token-level streaming, hook-based diff capture,
  `--max-turns` and `--max-budget` enforced, native file checkpointing.
- **codex** — the only backend that confines writes at the OS level under
  `--safe`. Whole-message streaming; diffs reconstructed from the git HEAD blob.
- **opencode** — native session fork and snapshot-backed revert; ignores
  `--effort`. A separate install, found on PATH.

## Safety

By default there is no sandbox: the agent can write anywhere you can and reach
the network. `--safe` confines edits to the project and screens destructive
commands — but only `codex` enforces this at the OS level. On claude and
opencode the screen matches paths and command patterns rather than parsing
shell, so a write redirected out of the project is not caught.

## Privacy

Airship runs entirely on localhost and adds no service of its own: no account,
no telemetry, no server. Whatever your chosen agent sends to its provider is
what it would send from your terminal, under credentials you already gave it.

## Requirements

Node 22.13 or later, and one of Claude Code, OpenAI Codex or OpenCode.
